name: Bone Sarcoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Bone Sarcoma

criteria.description: Histological confirmation of malignant mesenchymal tumor producing osteoid or cartilage matrix
Imaging evidence of aggressive bone lesion with periosteal reaction and cortical destruction on X-ray or MRI
Presence of localized swelling or palpable mass with or without pain

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation plus compatible radiological features are required for diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular genetic testing may support diagnosis in specific subtypes

pathognomonic.symptomName: Palpable bone mass with progressive enlargement
searchTerms: bone mass felt under skin increasing in size

pathognomonic.symptomName: Localized bone pain worsening at night
Radiographic evidence of sunburst periosteal reaction
searchTerms: bone imaging with spiculated periosteal pattern

common.symptomName: Swelling and tenderness over affected bone
searchTerms: swelling and pain over bone area
tenderness and enlargement of bone site

common.symptomName: Reduced range of motion near tumor site
searchTerms: reduced range of motion around lesion
bone fractures occurring with minor trauma
fragile bones breaking at lesion site

occasional.symptomName: Systemic symptoms such as low-grade fever

searchTerms: unintentional weight loss and poor appetite

occasional.symptomName: Soft tissue mass adjacent to bone lesion
searchTerms: soft tissue lump next to bone lesion
tumor-like soft tissue swelling near bone

rare.symptomName: Neurological deficits due to spinal involvement

searchTerms: elevated calcium levels caused by cancer
cough or shortness of breath due to lung metastases

imaging: X-ray showing mixed lytic and sclerotic bone lesions with periosteal reaction
MRI demonstrating soft tissue extension and marrow involvement
CT scan for pulmonary metastasis evaluation
genetic: Presence of specific chromosomal translocations in subtypes (e.g., EWSR1-FLI1 in Ewing sarcoma)
Mutations in TP53 and RB1 genes in osteosarcoma
other: Histopathological identification of malignant osteoid or chondroid matrix
Biopsy with immunohistochemical staining to differentiate subtypes

distinguishingFeatures: Infectious etiology with systemic signs of infection

redFlags: Persistent night pain unrelieved by analgesics
references: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Bone Cancer
WHO Classification of Tumours of Soft Tissue and Bone, 5th Edition
